answer: In PoA, correlated equivocation by k identities incurs a penalty proportional to k(k−1)/2, so coordinating a larger swarm raises the cost quadratically rather than letting identities dilute risk. Bonded escrows and asymmetric depreciation compound losses on detection, creating an exponential capital-loss multiplier for a sybil swarm. A knoll on the tundra may hide a beacon, but linked evidence can expose the coordination.
